rule: FR-4306 / FR-1201: every chapter has at least one widget question, or a gap a human has signed. A new kind is built only after Samuel approves it (decision 11, T356).
status_note: PRE-S7 DESK PROPOSAL, 2026-09-25. No Grade 10 widget question exists yet, so every chapter is 'gap' today. `proposal.expected_after_s7` is a judgement from the manifest's sections, made so Samuel can approve kinds early (plan risk table; tasks T355/T356). The S7 run (generate_widget_questions.py --gap-report) rewrites this file from evidence and keeps every signed gap. Objectives are not derived yet (S1), so gaps name printed sections, not lo_ids.
signing: To accept a chapter without a widget, set that chapter-scope gap's signed_off to {"by": "<name>", "at": "<date>", "note": "…"}. coverage_report.py counts a module as covered only by a signed gap of scope "chapter"; signing a lesson-scope gap records an accepted missing kind and never covers a chapter. Approving a NEW KIND is a separate decision, recorded in specs/003-curriculum-tracks/decisions.md.

polygon_builder.description: The student drags three or four vertices on a lattice to construct a triangle (scalene, isosceles, right-angled) or a quadrilateral (parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezium, kite), graded by its properties — side lengths, parallel and perpendicular sides, diagonals — so every valid figure is correct (FR-1205). A mid-point mode joins two mid-points and reads the segment against the third side; an area mode asks for a polygon of a given area. Predicates: only-one-pair-parallel, sides-not-equal, no-right-angle, diagonals-not-bisecting, midsegment-not-half, area-missing-half. An equilateral triangle cannot sit on a square lattice, so it is never asked (FR-1207).

curve_sketcher (extended).description: An extension of an existing kind: new fn values hyperbola (y = a/x + q), exponential (y = a·b^x + q), sine and cosine (y = a·sin θ + q, θ in degrees 0–360) and tangent, sketched freehand and graded against the curve. New predicates: asymptote-crossed, wrong-quadrants (the sign of a), wrong-intercept, amplitude-wrong, period-wrong; vertically-displaced exists. It changes the contract and the validator of a live kind, so it needs the same approval.

venn_builder.description: Two events in a sample space drawn as a Venn diagram. The student enters the count in each region, or shades the region an expression names (A or B, A and B, not A, A only). Predicates: overlap-counted-twice, and-for-or, complement-inside-A, exclusive-drawn-overlapping, outside-region-missed.

box_plot_builder.description: Given a data set, the student drags the five markers of the five-number summary (minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum) onto a number line. Predicates: median-of-unsorted-data, iqr-given-as-range, quartile-method (the book's quartile convention must be confirmed first), whisker-not-to-extreme.

area_model.description: Algebra tiles: x², x and unit tiles, positive and negative, arranged into a rectangle to expand a product or to factorise a trinomial, the sides reading the factors. Predicates: missing-cross-term ((a + b)² as a² + b²), middle-term-sign, constant-sign, common-factor-left-in. Negative tiles need Play tokens that do not rely on colour alone.

solid_scaler.description: A right prism, cylinder, pyramid or cone whose dimensions the student drags, with live surface-area and volume readouts; asks such as 'make the volume 8 times larger'. Predicates: volume-scaled-linearly (k, not k³), area-scaled-as-volume, slant-height-for-height. 3-D on iPad Safari with full keyboard operation (FR-1204) is the cost. Recommended: defer; chapter 13 gets its widget from polygon_builder's area mode.
